findings.current: Two S-rank Hunters—men who were practically the faces of their country—had died in a major incident. One of them had even been a comrade who had once fought alongside Magic Johnson on the same battlefield.
findings.defect: The singular “their country” implies that both Hunters represented the same country, although they were prominent figures of their respective nations.
findings.rationale: 한 나라의 얼굴이나 다름없는 characterizes each Hunter as effectively the face of a nation, not both as faces of one shared country.
findings.replacement: It was a major incident in which two S-rank Hunters—each practically the face of his own country—had died. One of them had even been a comrade who had once fought alongside Magic Johnson on the same battlefield.
findings.source: 한 나라의 얼굴이나 다름없는 S급 헌터가 둘이나 죽은 대사건, 심지어 그중 한 사람은 한때 매직 존슨과 같은 전장에서 싸웠던 전우이기도 했다.

findings.current: “It seems I went to a lot of trouble for nothing.”
findings.defect: The draft frames Johnson’s regret as wasted effort rather than regret over having followed Jin and learned an uncomfortable truth.
findings.rationale: 괜한 짓을 하다 means doing something unnecessary or ill-advised; here it specifically refers to Johnson’s decision to follow Jin.
findings.replacement: “Looks like I shouldn’t have followed you.”

findings.current: For Magic Johnson, this place was one of those times.
findings.defect: The sentence mismatches “place” with “times” and obscures that the truth confronting Johnson is what feels uncomfortable.
findings.rationale: 이 자리 refers to Johnson’s present situation and confrontation with the truth, not literally to a place categorized as a time.
findings.replacement: For Magic Johnson, this must have been one of those uncomfortable truths.
findings.source: 바로 지금 이 자리가 매직 존슨에게는 그럴 것이다.

findings.current: Everything that happened in the world was connected by invisible chains. If I didn’t want to fall one after another like dominoes, I had to prepare.
findings.defect: The draft incorrectly makes Jin himself the series of things that might fall like dominoes. The source refers to preventing interconnected events or circumstances from collapsing in succession.
findings.rationale: The omitted subject of 쓰러지다 follows the preceding reference to all events in the world; the singular narrator cannot logically fall “one after another.”
findings.replacement: Everything that happened in the world was connected by invisible links. To keep everything from toppling one after another like dominoes, I had to prepare.
findings.source: 세상에서 벌어지는 모든 일은 보이지 않는 고리로 연결되어 있다. 도미노처럼 줄줄이 쓰러지지 않으려면 준비해야 한다.

findings.current: It was a single word that meant he accepted.
findings.defect: Johnson’s preceding response is a full remark, not a single word.
findings.rationale: 한마디 denotes an utterance or remark here rather than literally one word.
findings.replacement: That single remark signaled his acceptance.

findings.defect: The generic phrasing drops the comic, embodied cue that Jin’s ears immediately perk up at the prospect of erasing Go Jun’s memory.
findings.rationale: 귀가 번쩍 뜨이다 is a vivid idiom indicating sudden, eager interest, which matters to the comedic beat.

findings.current: “It would obviously be difficult, but it isn’t impossible. Still, the stronger the target’s mental fortitude and the more memories you have to alter, the harder it becomes.”
findings.defect: The draft reduces 기억의 정도 to the number of memories, changing the stated mechanism from the extent or degree of the required alteration to a simple count.
findings.rationale: 정도 denotes degree or extent; it does not specifically state that difficulty depends on the numerical quantity of memories.
findings.replacement: “It would obviously be difficult, but it isn’t impossible. Still, the stronger the target’s mental fortitude and the more extensive the memories you have to alter, the harder it becomes.”
findings.source: 「당연히 어렵겠지만 불가능하지는 않아. 다만 대상이 강한 정신력을 지니고 있고, 조작해야 하는 기억의 정도에 따라 더 어려워지겠지.」

findings.current: After gathering my energy, I slowly swept my gaze across their corpse-pale faces before suddenly thrusting out a hand.
findings.defect: The draft reverses Jin’s action: he reins his qi back in after releasing his killing intent, rather than gathering or building up more energy.
findings.rationale: 갈무리하다 means to collect and contain or rein in what has been released; the surrounding action confirms that Jin is withdrawing his projected force.
findings.replacement: After reining in my qi, I slowly swept my gaze across their corpse-pale faces before suddenly thrusting out a hand.
findings.source: 기운을 갈무리한 나는 시체처럼 창백해진 세 놈의 얼굴을 천천히 쓸어보다 불쑥 손을 뻗었다.

findings.current:
“Your brain may be terrible, but how can you be so sinister and cunning?”

“……You son of a bitch.”

He wasn’t wrong, but it pissed me off.
findings.defect: “Your brain may be terrible” is an unnatural euphemism for calling Jin stupid, while the narration weakens the emphatic profanity in 개빡치네 and blunts the punchline.
findings.rationale: 머리는 나쁘다 directly insults Jin’s intelligence, and 개빡치네 is strongly profane rather than the milder “it pissed me off.”
findings.replacement:
“You’re an idiot, so how are you this devious and cunning?!”

“……You son of a bitch.”

He wasn’t wrong, but it pissed me the fuck off.
findings.source:
- 머리는 나쁜데, 어찌 이리도 음습하고 교활할 수가!

“……아니, 이 새끼가.”

맞는 말이긴 한데 개빡치네.

findings.current: Magic Gems were the essential driving force of the most advanced civilization in the world.
findings.defect: The draft invents a worldwide superlative and treats “civilization” as one uniquely most advanced society rather than referring to contemporary cutting-edge civilization and technology.
findings.rationale: 최첨단 means cutting-edge or state-of-the-art; it does not mean “the most advanced civilization in the world.”
findings.replacement: Magic Gems were now an essential power source for cutting-edge civilization.
findings.source: 현재의 마정석은 최첨단 문명의 필수 원동력.

findings.current: [^1]: *Jeongwan yewu* refers to the preferential treatment and influence former high-ranking government officials may receive when they become lawyers, especially through their old connections.
findings.defect: The footnote defines the practice too broadly as applying to former high-ranking government officials in general, obscuring its specific association with former judges and prosecutors receiving preferential treatment in legal proceedings.
findings.rationale: The joke specifically invokes a former chief prosecutor benefiting from the Korean legal convention known as 전관예우.
findings.replacement: [^1]: *Jeongwan yewu* is the unofficial preferential treatment often afforded to lawyers who formerly served as judges or prosecutors, particularly through their old professional connections.

findings.current: If the truth—that he was Cheon Taemin’s blood relative—were made public as well, the media would descend into chaos.
findings.defect: “Descend into chaos” unnaturally suggests institutional breakdown rather than the burst of excited media attention described by the source.
findings.rationale: 한바탕 난리를 피우다 means making a tremendous fuss or going into a frenzy, while 핏줄 emphasizes blood lineage.
findings.replacement: If the truth—that he was Cheon Taemin’s own flesh and blood—were made public as well, the media would undoubtedly go into a frenzy.
findings.source: 바로 그 천태민의 핏줄이라는 것까지 공개된다면 언론은 한바탕 난리를 피울 것이 분명하다.

summary: The draft contains one reversed physical action, several altered causal or pragmatic details, and localized register and terminology issues.
